Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The analyzed material consists of extracellular vesicles (EVs) isolated from human CSF via antibody-based immunocapture (affinity purification) and size-exclusion chromatography. Per precedence rules, the immunocapture method defines the scope as affinity-purified complex.

primary_biological_variables.matched_definition: Fallback category for studies where no clear perturbation or differential treatment axis is present in the proteomics comparison. This is not a mapping error when supported by evidence.
evidence: This study assesses the suitability of tetraspanin-based immunocapture (CD81, CD63, CD9 antibody mix) as a methodology for enrichment of EVs from CSF for proteomic biomarker discovery, comparing against SEC as an existing standard.

replicate_hints: four replicates for each of three different starting volumes
split into four replicates for protein digestion and subsequent proteomics
evidence: Proteomics was performed on technical replicates of immunocapture from a pool of CSF (made up of ten individuals), with four replicates for each of three different starting volumes (200 µL, 500 µL, 1000 µL). These were compared against SEC, for which a single isolation from 2 mL CSF was carried out from the same pool and split into four replicates for protein digestion and subsequent proteomics
Comparing SEC and immunocapture from a 500 µL equivalent starting volume
